from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES:',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA:',r.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,page in enumerate(r.pages)))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

p.rmdir()

strengths: The problem is well motivated: increasing the number of agents can improve reward availability while changing coordination difficulty, so a fixed few-to-more curriculum need not be appropriate.

Combining SPRL’s target-directed curriculum updates with critic-error prioritization is a simple, potentially useful contribution. Parameter sharing provides a practical mechanism for transferring policies across agent counts.

The evaluation covers Simple-Spread, a 20-player XOR game, eight SMAC-v2 scenarios, and two dense-reward BenchMARL tasks. Results show meaningful improvements over SPRLM on several sparse-reward tasks. Reporting target-task performance alongside training returns and generated curricula helps interpret these gains.

The appendix strengthens the empirical presentation through statistical comparisons, performance-threshold ablations, and hyperparameter tables. Pseudocode, implementation discussion, and a source-code link also support reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central interpretation of critic loss as learning progress is insufficiently justified. A perfectly evaluated but suboptimal policy can still have a nonzero policy gradient, contradicting the claim that converged value estimates imply no further policy updates. Conversely, stochastic returns can sustain large squared prediction errors without useful policy improvement. The experiments do not directly establish that the score predicts subsequent improvement or alleviates credit-assignment difficulty.

The variance analysis does not establish the claimed reduction in estimation uncertainty. Appendix A.3.4 computes dispersion across different sampled contexts, which mixes genuine task differences with sampling noise. It also compares episode returns against averaged squared residuals, quantities with different scales and units. Figures 7 and 10 therefore cannot, by themselves, substantiate the proposed mechanism; repeated estimates under fixed policies and contexts with matched sampling would be more informative.

Important baseline controls are missing. Simple-Spread uses an increasing Linear curriculum even though Section 6.1 explains why that direction fails; a more-to-fewer curriculum is a necessary comparison. ALPGMM and VACL also lack the proposed method’s explicit target-convergence requirement. Although the SPRLM comparison is informative, target-matched alternatives would better establish the benefit of adaptive critic-error scoring beyond increased exposure to the evaluation task.

The related-work discussion omits a close precedent: Prioritized Level Replay (Jiang et al., ICML 2021) already prioritizes training environments using value-error-derived scores. The combination with self-paced agent-count control can still constitute a contribution, but its originality and empirical advantage need clearer positioning relative to this prior approach.

Claims of consistent superiority exceed the reported evidence. Table 2 finds no significant improvement over SPRLM on XOR or over ALPGMM on Protoss 5v5 and 6v6; the dense-reward tasks show comparable performance. The supported conclusion is competitive performance with task-dependent gains, rather than uniform improvement over the strongest alternatives.

The implemented priority signal remains ambiguous: Equation 4 defines its target as a discounted return, whereas Appendix A.3.4 describes a one-step bootstrapped target. These produce different scores and noise properties. The manuscript should specify the actual target and normalization, along with baseline tuning and action-space handling in the variable-player XOR game. These are more consequential for reproduction than ordinary notation corrections.
